text:
New Jersey's four-game winning streak ended at Ball Arena, and it ended in the third period. Connor Brown's shorthanded goal in the first gave the Devils a 1-0 lead, and COL didn't level it until Gabriel Landeskog scored on the power play in the second. Then the third got away from NJD: Nazem Kadri and Parker Kelly scored 62 seconds apart, and Nathan MacKinnon and Jaden Schwartz added two more 30 seconds apart. Brown's second goal, at 15:35, only made the score look closer.

The scoreboard understated the gap. COL outshot NJD 44 to 22 on goal and had 80 shot attempts to 44. In expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, COL led 4.08 to 2.37, and our simulation of every shot gives the Avalanche a 76 percent chance of winning a replay. The second period was the clearest stretch, with COL out-chancing NJD 2.24 to 0.85. Devon Toews had a 22 percent look stopped by Jake Allen, who allowed 0.9 goals more than the shots against him deserved. Kelly's goal came on a 5 percent chance, the least likely of the night.

Kadri finished with a goal and an assist, as did Schwartz. Brent Burns added two assists on the way to second star, a long way from the 20th pick of 2003. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 20 of 22 for COL, close to what his shots called for. NJD had beaten COL 4-3 here on October 20, and now the two teams have split their first two meetings, while the Devils head home without the streak that had been carrying them.
